sample_unit: ophthalmologists (10 residents, 10 board-certified) answering 10 clinical scenarios

links.outcome: Proportion of additional citations that were hallucinated or incorrect with ChatGPT-4o assistance
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o assistance increased citation frequency (residents 0.24-0.98 per response; board-certified 0.12-0.68); approximately 44% of additional citations were hallucinated, nonexistent, or incorrect.
links.quote: Although ChatGPT-4o assistance increased citation frequency (residents: 0.24-0.98 per response, board-certified ophthalmologists: 0.12-0.68 per response, both P < 0.05), approximately 44% of these additional citations were identified as hallucinated references, nonexistent, or incorrect citations.

links.outcome: Clinician scores with versus without LLM assistance on coherency, factuality, comprehensiveness, safety
links.effect: Assistance improved coherency, comprehensiveness, and safety in both groups (all P<0.001); factuality showed no significant improvement (P=0.114 and 0.839); variability in factuality and safety increased.
links.quote: Assistance from ChatGPT-4o significantly improved evaluation scores for coherency, comprehensiveness, and safety among both residents and board-certified ophthalmologists (all, P < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Retrieval-augmented generation proposed to improve factual accuracy of LLM assistance in clinical education

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the effect of clinicians consulting an LLM (comparing clinician responses with and without AI assistance) on clinical reasoning, safety, and factuality across 10 vignette scenarios.
